<!-- generated by tools/gen-config.py from data/config/*.json (or the Director's .grammar). Do not edit by hand. -->

A Messages resource routes the messages of jobs and daemons to destinations: the catalog (job log), mail, files, syslog or the console.

## Examples

**Job messages to catalog, log file and mail on errors**

```text
Messages {
  Name = Standard
  Mail Command = "/usr/bin/bsmtp -h localhost -f \"Bareos <bareos@example.com>\" -s \"Bareos: %t %e of %c %l\" %r"
  Operator Command = "/usr/bin/bsmtp -h localhost -f \"Bareos <bareos@example.com>\" -s \"Bareos: Intervention needed for %j\" %r"
  Mail On Error = admin@example.com = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit
  Operator = admin@example.com = mount
  Console = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit
  Append = "/var/log/bareos/bareos.log" = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit
  Catalog = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit
}
```

## Directives

| Directive | Type | Default | | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Name](#d-name) | name |  |  | Name of the Messages resource; Jobs, the Director and daemons refer to it. |
| [Description](#d-description) | string |  |  | Free text describing the resource. |
| [Mail Command](#d-mailcommand) | string |  |  | Command that sends the mails of Mail, Mail On Error and Mail On Success. bsmtp is the usual choice. |
| [Operator Command](#d-operatorcommand) | string |  |  | Command for Operator messages (for example mount requests); same variables as Mail Command. |
| [Timestamp Format](#d-timestampformat) | string |  |  | strftime format of the time stamps of these messages. |
| [Syslog](#d-syslog) | message destination |  |  | Send messages to the system log. |
| [Mail](#d-mail) | message destination |  |  | Mail the messages to the addresses before the second = (comma separated) when the job ends, as one mail per job. |
| [Mail On Error](#d-mailonerror) | message destination |  |  | Like Mail, but the mail is only sent when the job did not terminate normally. |
| [Mail On Success](#d-mailonsuccess) | message destination |  |  | Like Mail, but only for jobs that terminated normally. |
| [File](#d-file) | message destination |  |  | Write the messages to a file, which is overwritten when the Director starts. |
| [Append](#d-append) | message destination |  |  | Append the messages to a file. |
| [Stdout](#d-stdout) | message destination |  |  | Print the messages on standard output of the daemon (mostly for debugging in the foreground). |
| [Stderr](#d-stderr) | message destination |  |  | Print the messages on standard error of the daemon. |
| [Director](#d-director) | message destination |  |  | Send the messages of a File or Storage Daemon to the Director named before the second =; only used in the daemons' own Messages resources. |
| [Console](#d-console) | message destination |  |  | Keep the messages for the consoles: they appear with the messages command (and automatically with autodisplay on). |
| [Operator](#d-operator) | message destination |  |  | Send the messages to the operator addresses through Operator Command, at once rather than at the end of the job. |
| [Catalog](#d-catalog) | message destination |  |  | Store the messages in the catalog (table Log); the job log shown by list joblog and by the GUI comes from there. |

### Name {#d-name}

Key: `name` · Type: name

Name of the Messages resource; Jobs, the Director and daemons refer to it.

```text
Messages {
  Name = "Standard"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add messages name=Standard
```

### Description {#d-description}

Key: `description` · Type: string

Free text describing the resource.

```text
Messages {
  Name = Standard
  Description = "Mail errors to the admins"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add messages name=Standard description="Mail errors to the admins"
```

### Mail Command {#d-mailcommand}

Key: `mailcommand` · Type: string

Command that sends the mails of Mail, Mail On Error and Mail On Success. bsmtp is the usual choice. Variables such as %r (recipients), %j (job name), %t (job type), %e (exit status), %c (client) and %d (Director) are replaced.

```text
Messages {
  Name = Standard
  Mail Command = "/usr/bin/bsmtp -h localhost -f \"Bareos <bareos@example.com>\" -s \"Bareos: %t %e of %c %l\" %r"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add messages name=Standard mailcommand="/usr/bin/bsmtp -h localhost -f \"Bareos <bareos@example.com>\" -s \"Bareos: %t %e of %c %l\" %r"
```

### Operator Command {#d-operatorcommand}

Key: `operatorcommand` · Type: string

Command for Operator messages (for example mount requests); same variables as Mail Command.

```text
Messages {
  Name = Standard
  Operator Command = "/usr/bin/bsmtp -h localhost -f bareos@example.com -s \"Bareos: Intervention needed for %j\" %r"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add messages name=Standard operatorcommand="/usr/bin/bsmtp -h localhost -f bareos@example.com -s \"Bareos: Intervention needed for %j\" %r"
```

### Timestamp Format {#d-timestampformat}

Key: `timestampformat` · Type: string

strftime format of the time stamps of these messages.

```text
Messages {
  Name = Standard
  Timestamp Format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add messages name=Standard timestampformat="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"
```

### Syslog {#d-syslog}

Key: `syslog` · Type: message destination

Send messages to the system log. A destination is followed by = and a comma separated list of message types: all, debug, abort, fatal, error, warning, info, saved, notsaved, skipped, mount, terminate, restored, security, alert, volmgmt, audit. !type removes a type, so "all, !skipped, !saved" means everything but the file lists.

```text
Messages {
  Name = Standard
  Syslog = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add messages name=Standard syslog="all, !skipped, !saved, !audit"
```

### Mail {#d-mail}

Key: `mail` · Type: message destination

Mail the messages to the addresses before the second = (comma separated) when the job ends, as one mail per job. A destination is followed by = and a comma separated list of message types: all, debug, abort, fatal, error, warning, info, saved, notsaved, skipped, mount, terminate, restored, security, alert, volmgmt, audit. !type removes a type, so "all, !skipped, !saved" means everything but the file lists.

```text
Messages {
  Name = Standard
  Mail = admin@example.com = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add messages name=Standard mail="admin@example.com = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit"
```

### Mail On Error {#d-mailonerror}

Key: `mailonerror` · Type: message destination

Like Mail, but the mail is only sent when the job did not terminate normally.

```text
Messages {
  Name = Standard
  Mail On Error = admin@example.com = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add messages name=Standard mailonerror="admin@example.com = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit"
```

### Mail On Success {#d-mailonsuccess}

Key: `mailonsuccess` · Type: message destination

Like Mail, but only for jobs that terminated normally.

```text

  Name = Standard
  Mail On Success = reports@example.com = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add messages name=Standard mailonsuccess="reports@example.com = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit"
```

### File {#d-file}

Key: `file` · Type: message destination

Write the messages to a file, which is overwritten when the Director starts. A destination is followed by = and a comma separated list of message types: all, debug, abort, fatal, error, warning, info, saved, notsaved, skipped, mount, terminate, restored, security, alert, volmgmt, audit. !type removes a type, so "all, !skipped, !saved" means everything but the file lists.

```text
Messages {
  Name = Standard
  File = "/var/log/bareos/last.log" = all, !skipped
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add messages name=Standard file="\"/var/log/bareos/last.log\" = all, !skipped"
```

### Append {#d-append}

Key: `append` · Type: message destination

Append the messages to a file. The usual log of Bareos is configured like this; rotate it with logrotate. A destination is followed by = and a comma separated list of message types: all, debug, abort, fatal, error, warning, info, saved, notsaved, skipped, mount, terminate, restored, security, alert, volmgmt, audit. !type removes a type, so "all, !skipped, !saved" means everything but the file lists.

```text
Messages {
  Name = Standard
  Append = "/var/log/bareos/bareos.log" = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add messages name=Standard append="\"/var/log/bareos/bareos.log\" = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit"
```

### Director {#d-director}

Key: `director` · Type: message destination

Send the messages of a File or Storage Daemon to the Director named before the second =; only used in the daemons' own Messages resources.

```text
Messages {
  Name = Standard
  Director = bareos-dir = all, !skipped, !restored
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add messages name=Standard director="bareos-dir = all, !skipped, !restored"
```

### Console {#d-console}

Key: `console` · Type: message destination

Keep the messages for the consoles: they appear with the messages command (and automatically with autodisplay on).

```text
Messages {
  Name = Standard
  Console = all, !skipped, !saved
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add messages name=Standard console="all, !skipped, !saved"
```

### Operator {#d-operator}

Key: `operator` · Type: message destination

Send the messages to the operator addresses through Operator Command, at once rather than at the end of the job. Typical for mount requests.

```text
Messages {
  Name = Standard
  Operator = admin@example.com = mount
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add messages name=Standard operator="admin@example.com = mount"
```

### Catalog {#d-catalog}

Key: `catalog` · Type: message destination

Store the messages in the catalog (table Log); the job log shown by list joblog and by the GUI comes from there.

```text
Messages {
  Name = Standard
  Catalog = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add messages name=Standard catalog="all, !skipped, !saved, !audit"
```

## Message types block {#block-types}

The types a destination lists after =, separated by commas; !type excludes one.

| Directive | Type | Default | | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [all](#b-types-all) | message type |  |  | Every message type; combine with !type to exclude some. |
| [debug](#b-types-debug) | message type |  |  | Debug messages. |
| [abort](#b-types-abort) | message type |  |  | A daemon aborts. |
| [fatal](#b-types-fatal) | message type |  |  | Fatal errors: the job is terminated. |
| [error](#b-types-error) | message type |  |  | Errors; the job goes on. |
| [warning](#b-types-warning) | message type |  |  | Warnings. |
| [info](#b-types-info) | message type |  |  | Informational messages. |
| [saved](#b-types-saved) | message type |  |  | One line per saved file (only with high verbosity). |
| [notsaved](#b-types-notsaved) | message type |  |  | Files that could not be saved. |
| [skipped](#b-types-skipped) | message type |  |  | Files skipped by the FileSet options (for example unchanged files). |
| [mount](#b-types-mount) | message type |  |  | Mount requests and volume mount messages. |
| [terminate](#b-types-terminate) | message type |  |  | The job end report. |
| [restored](#b-types-restored) | message type |  |  | One line per restored file. |
| [security](#b-types-security) | message type |  |  | Security relevant messages, such as failed authentication. |
| [alert](#b-types-alert) | message type |  |  | Alerts, for example from tape drives. |
| [volmgmt](#b-types-volmgmt) | message type |  |  | Volume management messages. |
| [audit](#b-types-audit) | message type |  |  | Audit log of console commands (Auditing in the Director). |
